title: Jonah and the Ember
premise: Astrid Kavanagh has spent her life in Hollowmere, a valley warded against magic, hiding her gift for speaking with beasts. When the old gods stir and the valley's wards crack, she flees north with Jonah, a runaway priest's apprentice who carries an ember of divine fire, and falls in with a ragtag found family of outcasts. Together they discover the god answering prayers is a devourer wearing King Aldric's crown, feeding on devotion to grow strong enough to consume the world's remaining wild magic. To save him, Astrid must unbind the king from the thing that wears him — but the unbinding demands a life freely given, and Jonah offers his before Astrid can stop him. In the end Astrid gives her voice instead, silencing her gift forever to sever the devourer from its host, and learns that love given up is still love kept.
about_author: Isandro Whitlock is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval bestiaries before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about quiet people carrying loud miracles, and live somewhere rainy with too many animals.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. We meet Hollowmere, its anti-magic wards, and Astrid secretly conversing with the miller's sick mare — a crime punishable by exile. A dying hawk delivers a warning: 'the gods are waking.' Emotional beat: the loneliness of a hidden self.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Fell From the Road
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Fleeing south with a burning ember lodged in his chest, Jonah collapses at the valley's edge; the wards reject him violently until Astrid pulls him through. Emotional beat: reluctant compassion overriding fear of discovery.

chapters.title: What the Ember Wants
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The ember speaks through Jonah in dreams, naming Astrid by a title she doesn't know: 'Listener.' The village elders notice the ward-scar on his skin. Emotional beat: two secrets recognizing each other.

chapters.title: Wardfall
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. The valley's ancient wards shatter overnight; magic floods in like cold water, and the first answered prayer arrives — a harvest godling that devours a field and the farmer who prayed to it. Emotional beat: home becoming unlivable.

chapters.title: Exile's Road
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Branded as the cause, the pair flee north together, bickering, terrified, bound by necessity. They survive their first ambush by bandits using Astrid's beast-craft. Emotional beat: strangers becoming allies.

chapters.title: The Tollhouse of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. They shelter with Maren, a disgraced hedge-witch, and Bramble, a talking crow who claims he once served a god. First hints that the ember is a fragment of a murdered deity. Emotional beat: found family begins to form.

chapters.title: Prayers With Teeth
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. In the city of Vael Crossing they witness mass devotion to the 'Crowned God' — and watch a supplicant burn alive mid-prayer, his faith harvested. Emotional beat: horror at worship weaponized.

chapters.title: The Listener's Burden
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Astrid hears the land itself screaming under the Crowned God's pull. She confesses her gift fully to Jonah; he tells her the ember chose her long before they met. Emotional beat: intimacy through truth-telling.

chapters.title: A Court of Crows
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. The group infiltrates a secret conclave of old-faith survivors led by the crow-god's remnant. They learn the devourer's true name and that it wears King Aldric like armor. Emotional beat: hope with a price tag attached.

chapters.title: The King Who Is Not Home
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Infiltrating the palace, they glimpse Aldric — a hollow man puppeted by divinity, weeping behind eyes that aren't his. Jonah recognizes the devourer's hunger from his own ember. Emotional beat: pity for the enemy.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Undercroft
chapters.summary: Bramble's POV. One conclave member sells them out; Maren is captured covering their escape, and the ember flares, marking Jonah publicly as a god-bearer. Emotional beat: guilt and the cost of trust.

chapters.title: Hunted Through Holy Ground
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. A chase across consecrated countryside where every church bell betrays their position; Astrid turns the beasts of the wilds into their shield. Emotional beat: her gift, once shameful, becomes salvation.

chapters.title: The Drowned Chapel
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Hidden in a flooded ruin, Jonah communes with the ember and learns the unbinding rite requires a soul freely offered. He begins planning in secret. Emotional beat: quiet, terrible resolve.

chapters.title: What Maren Taught the Dark
chapters.summary: Maren's POV, captive. Interrogated by the devourer's high priest, Maren stalls, lies, and plants doubt among the faithful — buying the others time at brutal cost. Emotional beat: defiance as love.

chapters.title: The Ember's Confession
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. The ember reveals it was torn from the devourer when the gods imprisoned it — it is both key and bait, and it wants to go home. Astrid realizes Jonah intends to be the offering. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into determination.

chapters.title: Storming the Crown
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The found family, reunited with freed Maren and the crow-conclave, assaults the capital during the Feast of Answered Prayers. Emotional beat: camaraderie before catastrophe.

chapters.title: The Devourer Unmasked
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Confrontation in the throne room: the devourer sheds Aldric's body partially, revealing its vast, starving shape. It offers Astrid everything — her voice returned tenfold, her valley restored — if she joins it. Emotional beat: temptation made flesh.

chapters.title: The Offering
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Jonah steps forward to give his life; Astrid interposes, choosing instead to surrender her beast-speech — the very gift the devourer covets — as the freely given sacrifice. Emotional beat: love choosing loss over loss choosing for them.

chapters.title: Unbinding
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The rite tears god from king; the devourer, severed from worship and denied its prize, collapses inward. Aldric wakes, mortal and broken, in Jonah's arms. Emotional beat: catharsis after agony.

chapters.title: Silence Where the Songs Were
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Grieving her lost gift, Astrid can no longer hear the beasts — but a crow lands on her shoulder and stays anyway, wordless. Emotional beat: mourning that softens into acceptance.

chapters.title: The King's Debt
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Aldric, restored, repeals the persecution of gifted folk and asks what he owes them. The family asks not for gold but for a valley re-warded — this time with room inside it for magic. Emotional beat: justice without vengeance.

chapters.title: Home, Rewritten
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. The found family returns to a Hollowmere where wards now shelter rather than exclude. Astrid cannot speak to animals, but Bramble speaks for them all, and Jonah's hand finds hers. Final beat: survival cost something, and what remains is worth keeping.
